f.title: Conduct EPPV for six months after launch of a new drug, collecting ADRs from all using institutions and taking safety measures
f.statement: Early Post-marketing Phase Vigilance (EPPV) covers safety assurance activities conducted within the 6 months just after marketing of a new drug: it is imposed on the marketing authorisation holder to collect adverse drug reactions in all medical institutions where the drug is used and to take safety measures, with the aim of promoting rational use and taking prompt action to prevent serious ADRs. EPPV is specified as a condition of approval.
f.clause: 3. List of products subject to Early Post-marketing Phase Vigilance
f.applicability: Superseded version (historical October 2009 bulletin; no successor named in the text or catalog). Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Safety Information No. 262 (MHLW Pharmaceutical and Food Safety Bureau, October 2009); English translation by PMDA for information purposes only (the Japanese text prevails); MAH duties only captured
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Safety intake & collection

rows.deadline: Six months after marketing of the new drug
rows.quote:
Early Post-marketing Phase Vigilance (EPPV) was established in 2001. This unique system for
new drugs refers to any safety assurance activities that are conducted within a period of 6 months
just after marketing of a new drug. It is imposed that its Marketing Authorization Holder collects
the adverse drug rections (ADRs) in all of the medical institutions where the drugs are used and
takes safety measures. The aim of the EPPV is to promote the rational use of the drug in medical
treatments, and to take prompt actions for the prevention of the serious adverse drug reactions.
EPPV is specified as a condition of approval.
